column8: The repeated positional VALUES insert admits only markers at their exact left-to-right positions over a full configured column list, binds each execute vector to one clustered signed-BIGINT row, and encodes Go-byte-exact record keys and row values. The original also covers INSERT SELECT and the prepared plan-cache hit counter on an `int PRIMARY KEY` table, and asserts persisted rows through a live server; those remain open here and belong to the dependent server and live-proof slices.

The repeated point arithmetic update binds the assigned value before the handle, reads the stored column at the transaction start timestamp, adds with the same overflow boundary as Go's signed PLUS, and publishes one exists-asserted row only when the value changes. The original also covers the prepared plan-cache hit counter and asserts persisted rows through a live server; general SET expressions, matched-row bookkeeping, and persistence remain open here.

A multi-row INSERT reports one row per added record and a point UPDATE reports a row only when the stored value changes, so an unchanged or missing row reports zero. The original also pins ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE's two-row accounting, the ClientFoundRows capability that makes an unchanged row count, and DELETE/REPLACE cases; none of those are admitted by this bounded write path and remain open.

One clustered signed-BIGINT row round-trips through the record key plus new-format value, byte-exact against tablecodec/rowcodec output for the whole signed handle domain and every compact integer width. The original also covers non-integer datums, NULL columns, column-not-found handling, and timezone-dependent temporal values; those stay with the codec waves and remain open here.

Signed integer column payloads and their not-null column-ID sort are byte-exact against Go, including the large-row format a column ID above one byte forces into u32 ID and offset metadata. The original also covers every other column type, NULL partitions, checksums, and reuse behavior, which remain open.
